title: About 5% of Your Power Never Arrives #shorts
summary: Transmission and distribution losses averaged about 5% of the electricity sent through US lines in 2018-2022 (EIA).
sources: Transmission and distribution losses averaged about 5% of the electricity transmitted and distributed in the US in 2018 through 2022 (EIA FAQ, updated 7 Nov 2023): https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=105&t=3

Supply must match demand for the grid to stay stable; transformers step voltage up and down between the power plant, long-distance lines and distribution lines; the Eastern and Western interconnections are linked to Canada's grid (EIA, Electricity explained: delivery to consumers): https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/electricity/delivery-to-consumers.php

Nearly 160,000 miles of high-voltage power lines; a balancing authority ensures, in real time, that power system demand and supply are finely balanced (EIA, Today in Energy, 20 Jul 2016): https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=27152

scenes.narration: About {5%|five percent} of the power sent to you never arrives.
It leaves a power plant, and a transformer cranks the voltage up.
High voltage loses less over long distances. Still, some energy leaks away along the lines.
Then substations and the can on your pole step it down.
So for every hundred units sent, about five never make it. Five percent, gone.
